tools.name: memory_status
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether MemoryRouter is connected, which opaque vault binding is active, or how many memories/tokens the connected vault contains. Does not reveal the memory key.

tools.name: forget_all_memories
tools.description: Use this only after the user explicitly requests a full-vault deletion, receives a permanent whole-vault warning, and provides the exact confirmation phrase in a later turn. Permanently deletes every memory in the OAuth-selected vault. This cannot delete one memory; use delete_memories for specific

tools.name: consolidate_memories
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to consolidate, reflect on, or organize their memories, or when memory_status or a search result reports that consolidation is available. tools.name: commit_reflections
tools.description: Use this to complete a consolidation started with consolidate_memories. Submits the reflection entries you wrote for the checked-out batch. tools.name: inspect_memory
tools.description: Use this when exact details or provenance matter: when the user asks why the assistant believes something, or wants to see the source memories behind a reflection. tools.name: delete_memories
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to delete specific memories and confirms after seeing what will be deleted. tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this legacy compatibility alias when a client explicitly requests a tool named search. It searches the OAuth-selected MemoryRouter vault without modifying it. For normal ChatGPT recall, prefer search_memories; this tool does not provide citable item permalinks or Company Knowledge fetch support.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_memories" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "search_memories" stacks urgency/override words (important, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
